questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं :

कथन I : आर्थिक विकास के लिए चीन द्वारा अपनायी गयी आर्थिक नीतियों ने इसकी अर्थव्यवस्था की जड़ता को तोड़ने में सहायता प्रदान की ।

कथन II : चीन के आर्थिक विकास ने पर्यावरण निम्नीकरण और भ्रष्टाचार को बढ़ावा दिया ।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के संदर्भ में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Given below are two statements :

Statement-I : The economic policies implemented by China helped to break the stagnation of its economy.

Statement-II : Economic development of China also increased environmental degradation and corruption.

In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.A: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सत्य हैं ।
options.B: कथन I और कथन II दोनों असत्य हैं ।
options.C: कथन I सत्य है, परंतु कथन II असत्य है ।
options.D: कथन I असत्य है, परंतु कथन II सत्य है ।

options_english.A: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
options_english.B: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
options_english.C: Statement-I is true, but Statement-II is false.
options_english.D: Statement-I is false, but Statement-II is true.

questions.solution: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true. China adopted gradual economic reforms — opening Special Economic Zones, encouraging foreign investment, and moving away from a rigid planned economy — which effectively broke economic stagnation and led to rapid GDP growth. However, this rapid industrialisation also caused severe environmental degradation such as air and water pollution, and created opportunities for widespread corruption within the communist party and state machinery. Hence option (A) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सत्य हैं। चीन ने विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्रों की स्थापना, विदेशी निवेश को प्रोत्साहन तथा नियोजित अर्थव्यवस्था से क्रमिक दूरी बनाकर आर्थिक सुधार किए जिससे आर्थिक जड़ता टूटी। साथ ही तीव्र औद्योगीकरण से पर्यावरण निम्नीकरण और भ्रष्टाचार भी बढ़ा। अतः विकल्प (A) सही है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन से कारण के फलस्वरूप 1952 में आंध्र राज्य का गठन हुआ ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is the reason that led to the formation of Andhra state in 1952 ?

options.A: औपनिवेशिक शासन की समाप्ति के बाद भारतीय राज्यों की आंतरिक सीमाओं के पुनर्निर्धारण की आवश्यकता को महसूस करना ।
options.B: 1920 के नागपुर अधिवेशन में भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस ने यह मान लिया था कि आजादी के बाद राज्यों का पुनर्गठन भाषा के आधार पर किया जायेगा ।
options.C: कांग्रेस नेता, पोट्टी श्रीरामुलु की मृत्यु, जिसके कारण व्यापक अव्यवस्था फैली और विरोध में मद्रास के कई विधायकों ने त्यागपत्र दिया ।
options.D: पुराने मद्रास राज्य के तमिल बोलने वाले लोगों ने भाषा के आधार पर राज्य के पुनर्सीमांकन की माँग की ।

options_english.A: Realising the need to reorganise the internal boundaries of Indian states at the end of colonial rule.
options_english.B: Reorganisation of the Indian National Congress on the basis of linguistic principle after Nagpur session in 1920.
options_english.C: Death of the Congress leader, Potti Sriramulu which caused great unrest and led to resignation of several legislators of Madras in protest.
options_english.D: The Tamil speaking people of old Madras province demanding the reorganisation of state on the basis of language.

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The immediate cause for the creation of the separate state of Andhra in 1952 was the death of Telugu leader Potti Sriramulu after a 56-day fast-unto-death demanding a separate Telugu-speaking state. His death triggered widespread riots and unrest across Madras, forcing Prime Minister Nehru to announce the formation of Andhra Pradesh — India's first state carved on linguistic lines. Options A and B describe background context but were not the direct trigger, and option D refers to Tamil speakers, not Telugu speakers.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) सही है। 1952 में आंध्र राज्य के गठन का तात्कालिक कारण कांग्रेस नेता पोट्टी श्रीरामुलु की मृत्यु थी जो 56 दिन के आमरण अनशन के बाद हुई। इनकी मृत्यु के बाद व्यापक अव्यवस्था फैली और मद्रास के कई विधायकों ने त्यागपत्र दिया। इससे विवश होकर प्रधानमंत्री नेहरू ने भाषा के आधार पर आंध्र राज्य के गठन की घोषणा की।

questions.text: चीन द्वारा अपने आर्थिक संकट के समाधान के लिये कौन सा उपाय अपनाया गया ?
questions.text_english: Which measure was adopted by China to solve its economic crisis ?

options.A: सोवियत संघ की तरह, चीन ने 'शॉक थेरेपी' को अपनाया ।
options.B: विश्व के अधिकांश विकासशील देशों के साथ संबंध बनाकर चीन ने अपने आर्थिक एकांतवास को समाप्त किया ।
options.C: अपनी अर्थव्यवस्था के विकास के लिये चीन ने चरणबद्ध तरीके से निजीकरण के लिए अपनी अर्थव्यवस्था को खोला ।
options.D: चीन ने आयात की अपेक्षा निर्यात को अधिक बढ़ावा दिया ।

options_english.A: Like USSR, China also followed 'Shock Therapy'.
options_english.B: China ended its economic isolation with the establishment of relations with most of the developing countries of the World.
options_english.C: China opened its economy for privatisation step by step for the development of its economy.
options_english.D: China focused more on export as compared to import.

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. Unlike the Soviet Union which adopted the abrupt and painful 'Shock Therapy', China took a gradual, phased approach to economic reform. It opened Special Economic Zones selectively, allowed limited private enterprise, attracted foreign investment step by step, and maintained state control over key sectors — a strategy often called 'socialism with Chinese characteristics'. This measured approach prevented economic collapse and delivered sustained growth. Option A is incorrect as China explicitly avoided Shock Therapy.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) सही है। सोवियत संघ के विपरीत चीन ने अचानक शॉक थेरेपी नहीं अपनाई। इसके बजाय उसने चरणबद्ध तरीके से विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्र स्थापित किए, सीमित निजीकरण को अनुमति दी और विदेशी निवेश को क्रमिक रूप से आमंत्रित किया। इसे 'चीनी विशेषताओं वाला समाजवाद' कहा गया।
questions.chapter: दो ध्रुवीयता का अंत / The End of Bipolarity

questions.text: 'आया राम गया राम' के जुमले से संबंधित राज्य की पहचान कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Identify the State with which the phrase 'Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram' is related to.
questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The phrase 'Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram' originated in Haryana in 1967 when a legislator named Gaya Lal changed his party affiliation three times in a single day. This phrase became a popular expression in Indian politics to describe political defections and floor-crossing by elected representatives. It eventually led to the passage of the Anti-Defection Law under the 52nd Constitutional Amendment in 1985.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) सही है। 'आया राम गया राम' का जुमला 1967 में हरियाणा से उत्पन्न हुआ जब गया लाल नामक एक विधायक ने एक ही दिन में तीन बार दल बदला। यह जुमला भारतीय राजनीति में दल-बदल की प्रवृत्ति का प्रतीक बन गया और अंततः 1985 में दल-बदल विरोधी कानून का मार्ग प्रशस्त हुआ।

questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं – जिनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है । इन कथनों को ध्यान से पढ़िए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से उत्तर के रूप में सही विकल्प चुनिए ।

अभिकथन (A) : पूरे विश्व में पुराने 'कल्याणकारी राज्य' को अधिक महत्व दिया जा रहा है ।

कारण (R) : वैश्वीकरण के कारण राज्य के लोक कल्याणकारी कार्यों की भूमिका में कमी आयी है और बाज़ार, आर्थिक और सामाजिक प्राथमिकताओं का प्रमुख निर्धारक बन गया है ।
questions.text_english:
Given below are two statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Read these statements carefully and choose the correct answer from the options (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

Assertion (A) : All over the world, the old 'welfare state' is getting more importance.

Reason (R) : Due to globalisation, the state withdraws from many of its earlier welfare functions and the market has become the prime determinant of economic and social priorities.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है ।

options_english.A: Both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are true, but the Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The Assertion (A) is false because globalisation has actually led to a decline in the importance of the welfare state — not an increase. As market forces dominate, governments are under pressure to reduce social spending, leading critics to argue that welfare states are under threat. The Reason (R) is true: globalisation does cause states to withdraw from welfare functions as market becomes the primary allocator of resources. Since A is false and R is true, option (C) is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) सही है। अभिकथन (A) असत्य है क्योंकि वैश्वीकरण के कारण कल्याणकारी राज्य का महत्व घटा है, बढ़ा नहीं। कारण (R) सत्य है — वैश्वीकरण के कारण राज्य अपने कल्याणकारी कार्यों से पीछे हट रहा है और बाजार प्राथमिकताओं का निर्धारक बन गया है।

questions.text: देसी रियासतों के विषय में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन असत्य है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about the princely states ?

options.A: देसी रियासतों पर राजाओं का शासन था ।
options.B: ब्रिटिश राज की समाप्ति के बाद समस्त देसी रियासतों ने भारत में शामिल होना स्वीकार कर लिया था ।
options.C: देसी रियासतों के राजाओं ने ब्रिटिश की सर्वोच्च सत्ता को स्वीकार कर लिया था और इसके अंतर्गत वे अपने राज्य के घरेलू मामलों का शासन चलाते थे ।
options.D: ब्रिटिश सत्ता की समाप्ति के बाद देसी रियासतें भारत या पाकिस्तान में शामिल होने या अपनी स्वतन्त्र हैसियत बनाए रखने के लिए आज़ाद थीं ।

options_english.A: Princely states were ruled by the princes.
options_english.B: All the princely states had accepted to be an integral part of India after the end of British rule.
options_english.C: The princes of princely states accepted British supremacy and enjoyed some form of control over their internal affairs.
options_english.D: After the end of British paramountcy, the provinces were free to join either India or Pakistan or remain independent.

questions.solution: Option (B) is the incorrect statement and hence the correct answer. Not all princely states willingly accepted integration into India after independence. While most did accede, some states like Hyderabad, Junagadh, and Kashmir were reluctant or initially refused. The Indian government had to use diplomatic pressure, military action (Police Action in Hyderabad), and negotiation to bring them into the Union. Options A, C, and D are factually correct descriptions of princely states under British paramountcy.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (B) असत्य कथन है। सभी देसी रियासतों ने स्वेच्छा से भारत में विलय नहीं किया। हैदराबाद, जूनागढ़ और कश्मीर जैसी रियासतें प्रारंभ में विलय से हिचकिचा रही थीं। हैदराबाद में तो पुलिस एक्शन द्वारा बलपूर्वक विलय कराना पड़ा।

questions.text:
सूची-I का सूची-II से सही मिलान कीजिए और दिए गए कोड से उत्तर का सही विकल्प चुनिए :

सूची-I
(a) मानवाधिकारों का हनन
(b) 'मैड-काऊ' बीमारी
(c) निःशस्त्रीकरण संधि
(d) 9/11 का आतंकी हमला

सूची-II
(i) ब्रिटेन
(ii) केमिकल वेपन्स कनवेन्शन
(iii) अमरीका का वर्ल्ड ट्रेड सेंटर
(iv) कुवैत पर इराक का हमला
questions.text_english:
Match List-I with List-II correctly and choose the correct answer from the codes given below :

List-I
(a) Violation of Human Rights
(b) 'Mad-Cow' disease
(c) Disarmament Treaty
(d) 9/11 terrorist attack

List-II
(i) Britain
(ii) Chemical weapons convention
(iii) World Trade Centre in America
(iv) Iraq's invasion of Kuwait
questions.solution: Option (A) is correct: (a) Violation of Human Rights – (iv) Iraq's invasion of Kuwait (which involved massive human rights violations against Kuwaiti civilians); (b) 'Mad-Cow' disease – (i) Britain (the BSE/Mad Cow epidemic originated in Britain); (c) Disarmament Treaty – (ii) Chemical Weapons Convention (the major disarmament treaty banning chemical weapons); (d) 9/11 terrorist attack – (iii) World Trade Centre in America (the twin towers of the WTC in New York were the primary target on September 11, 2001).
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (A) सही है: (a) मानवाधिकारों का हनन – (iv) कुवैत पर इराक का हमला; (b) मैड-काऊ बीमारी – (i) ब्रिटेन; (c) निःशस्त्रीकरण संधि – (ii) केमिकल वेपन्स कनवेन्शन; (d) 9/11 का आतंकी हमला – (iii) अमरीका का वर्ल्ड ट्रेड सेंटर।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित घटनाओं को कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए :

(i) पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री राजीव गांधी की हत्या ।
(ii) केंद्र में प्रथम गैर-कांग्रेसी गठबंधन सरकार का गठन ।
(iii) 16वाँ लोकसभा चुनाव ।
(iv) मंडल आयोग द्वारा अपनी सिफारिशें प्रस्तुत की गईं ।

सही विकल्प चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following events in chronological order :

(i) Assassination of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.
(ii) Formation of the First Non-Congress coalition government at the centre.
(iii) Sixteenth Lok Sabha elections.
(iv) The Mandal Commission gave its recommendations.

Choose the correct option :
questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The correct chronological order is: (iv) Mandal Commission submitted its recommendations in 1980; (ii) Formation of First Non-Congress coalition government at the centre in 1977 under Morarji Desai — wait, re-checking: VP Singh government in 1989 was the first truly non-Congress coalition; (i) Assassination of Rajiv Gandhi in 1991; (iii) 16th Lok Sabha elections in 2014. So the correct order is (iv) 1980, (ii) 1989, (i) 1991, (iii) 2014, which is option (C).
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (C) सही है। सही कालक्रम: (iv) मंडल आयोग की सिफारिशें — 1980; (ii) केंद्र में पहली गैर-कांग्रेसी गठबंधन सरकार — 1989; (i) राजीव गांधी की हत्या — 1991; (iii) 16वाँ लोकसभा चुनाव — 2014।
questions.chapter: भारतीय राजनीति: नए बदलाव / Recent Developments in Indian Politics

questions.text: 'प्रिवी पर्स' को समाप्त करने वाले प्रधानमंत्री का नाम चुनिए ।
questions.text_english: Choose the name of the Prime Minister who abolished 'Privy Purse'.
questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. Privy Purse referred to the annual payments made to former rulers of princely states as part of their accession agreements with India. Prime Minister Indira Gandhi abolished the Privy Purse system in 1971 through the 26th Constitutional Amendment as part of her populist 'Garibi Hatao' campaign. This move was also aimed at removing the special privileges enjoyed by the former royals and was a significant step in consolidating Indira Gandhi's political position.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (D) सही है। प्रिवी पर्स भारत में देसी रियासतों के पूर्व शासकों को दी जाने वाली वार्षिक राशि थी। इंदिरा गांधी ने 1971 में 26वें संविधान संशोधन के द्वारा प्रिवी पर्स को समाप्त किया। यह उनके 'गरीबी हटाओ' कार्यक्रम का हिस्सा था।
questions.chapter: लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था का संकट / Crisis of Democratic Order

questions.text: उस कथन को चुनिए जो वैश्वीकरण की अवधारणा को सर्वश्रेष्ठ तरीके से व्यक्त करता है ।
questions.text_english: Choose the statement that best describes the concept of globalisation.

options.A: विश्व के देशों के बीच वस्तुओं, पूँजी, व्यक्तियों और विचारों की आवाजाही के कारण तीव्र एकीकरण या पारस्परिक निर्भरता की बढ़ती प्रक्रिया ।
options.B: राजनीतिक क्षेत्र में वैश्वीकरण ने राज्य की क्षमताओं को बढ़ाया है ।
options.C: वैश्वीकरण ने उपभोक्ताओं को सीमित विकल्पों में से चुनने की स्वतंत्रता प्रदान की है ।
options.D: वैश्वीकरण ने व्यक्तियों को रोज़गार के विभिन्न अवसर कम किए हैं ।

options_english.A: The process of rapid integration or inter-connection among countries of the world through the flow of goods, capital, people and ideas.
options_english.B: Globalisation has increased states capabilities in the political field.
options_english.C: Globalisation has given freedom to consumers to choose from limited alternatives.
options_english.D: Globalisation has reduced the various opportunities of employment to the people.

questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. Globalisation is best understood as the process of increasing interconnectedness and integration among countries driven by the free flow of goods, capital, people, technology, and ideas across national boundaries. This is the most comprehensive and standard academic definition. Option B is incorrect as globalisation generally constrains state power; option C is wrong as globalisation actually expands consumer choices, not limits them; option D is partially contested as globalisation both creates and destroys jobs depending on context.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (A) सही है। वैश्वीकरण को सर्वोत्तम रूप से वस्तुओं, पूँजी, व्यक्तियों और विचारों के मुक्त प्रवाह के कारण देशों के बीच बढ़ती परस्पर निर्भरता और एकीकरण की प्रक्रिया के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है। यह सबसे व्यापक और मानक परिभाषा है।
questions.chapter: वैश्वीकरण / Globalisation

questions.text: उस पार्टी की पहचान कीजिए जिसकी 2009 से 2019 तक के आम चुनावों में लोक सभा सीटों में लगातार बढ़ोतरी हुई ।
questions.text_english: Identify the political party which has had a continuous growth in its Lok Sabha seats in the General Elections from 2009 to 2019.

options.D: कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी ऑफ इंडिया (सी पी आई)

questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) showed consistent growth in Lok Sabha seats across the three general elections: in 2009 it won 116 seats, in 2014 it won a decisive 282 seats (majority on its own), and in 2019 it won 303 seats. The INC showed a decline from 206 seats in 2009 to 44 in 2014 and 52 in 2019. Shiv Sena and CPI did not show consistent growth during this period.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (B) सही है। भारतीय जनता पार्टी (BJP) ने 2009 से 2019 तक के आम चुनावों में लगातार वृद्धि दर्शाई: 2009 में 116, 2014 में 282 और 2019 में 303 सीटें। INC की सीटें घटती रहीं।
questions.chapter: भारतीय राजनीति: नए बदलाव / Recent Developments in Indian Politics

questions.text: परमाणु अप्रसार सन्धि का संबंध है –
questions.text_english: Nuclear non-proliferation Treaty refers to :

options.A: परमाणु ऊर्जा के शांतिपूर्ण प्रयोग से ।
options.D: परमाणु हथियारों के ज़खीरे में कमी करना ।

questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. The Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), opened for signature in 1968, aims to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons to new states and to work toward the eventual reduction and elimination of nuclear weapons stockpiles held by existing nuclear powers. While it also promotes peaceful uses of nuclear energy, its core purpose is non-proliferation and disarmament — making reduction of stockpiles the most precise description. Option B (spread) would be an incorrect framing as NPT opposes proliferation.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प (D) सही है। परमाणु अप्रसार संधि (NPT) का मुख्य उद्देश्य परमाणु हथियारों के प्रसार को रोकना और परमाणु शक्ति संपन्न देशों के हथियारों के ज़खीरे में कमी करना है। यह संधि 1968 में हस्ताक्षर के लिए खुली थी।
questions.chapter: समकालीन विश्व में सुरक्षा / Security in the Contemporary World

questions.text: योजना आयोग की स्थापना के किन्हीं दो उद्देश्यों को उजागर कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Highlight any two objectives of establishing Planning Commission.

key_points: To assess the material, capital and human resources of the country and investigate the possibilities of augmenting deficient resources.
To formulate a plan for the most effective and balanced utilisation of the country's resources and to determine priorities for development.

questions.solution: The Planning Commission, established in 1950, served two key objectives. First, it was created to assess and mobilise the country's resources — including material, capital, and human resources — and to investigate ways of increasing resources that were insufficient for development needs. Second, it was tasked with formulating a comprehensive plan for the most effective and balanced utilisation of those resources, setting out priorities to guide national development so that economic growth would be equitable and sustained across all sectors and regions of India.
questions.solution_hindi: 1950 में स्थापित योजना आयोग के दो प्रमुख उद्देश्य थे। प्रथम, देश के भौतिक, पूँजीगत और मानवीय संसाधनों का आकलन करना और कमी वाले संसाधनों को बढ़ाने के उपाय खोजना। द्वितीय, संसाधनों के सर्वोत्तम एवं संतुलित उपयोग की योजना बनाना तथा विकास की प्राथमिकताएँ निर्धारित करना ताकि आर्थिक विकास न्यायसंगत हो।
questions.chapter: नियोजित विकास की राजनीति / Politics of Planned Development

questions.text: दक्षिण एशियाई क्षेत्र की भौगोलिक विशिष्टता किस प्रकार इसके सांस्कृतिक अनूठेपन को निर्धारित करती है ? स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: How does the natural insularity of South Asian region determine its cultural distinctiveness ? Explain.

key_points: South Asia is naturally insulated by the Himalayas in the north, the Indian Ocean in the south, and deserts in the west, creating a distinct geographical unit.

This natural isolation fostered a unique shared civilisational heritage — common religions like Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, similar languages, shared foods, art, and cultural traditions — that differ from the rest of Asia.

questions.solution: South Asia's unique geographical setting acts as a natural barrier that has historically isolated it from other parts of the world, creating a distinct cultural zone. The towering Himalayan ranges in the north, the vast Indian Ocean in the south, and the Thar Desert in the west form natural boundaries that limited outside cultural penetration. Within this insulated space, a rich civilisational tradition developed — shared religions such as Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism, interrelated languages, similar arts and architecture, and common social customs — giving South Asia a cultural identity distinct from East Asia, Southeast Asia, or the Middle East.
questions.solution_hindi: दक्षिण एशिया की भौगोलिक विशेषता इसे अन्य क्षेत्रों से अलग करती है। उत्तर में हिमालय, दक्षिण में हिंद महासागर और पश्चिम में थार मरुस्थल प्राकृतिक सीमाएँ बनाते हैं जो बाहरी सांस्कृतिक प्रभावों को सीमित करती हैं। इसी भौगोलिक अलगाव में हिंदू धर्म, बौद्ध धर्म, जैन धर्म, समान भाषाएँ, कला और सामाजिक परंपराएँ पनपीं, जो दक्षिण एशिया की सांस्कृतिक विशिष्टता का आधार हैं।
questions.chapter: दक्षिण एशिया में समकालीन राजनीति / Contemporary South Asia
questions.topic: South Asia — Geographical and Cultural Identity

questions.text: पर्यावरणीय निम्नीकरण के लिए उत्तरदायी किन्हीं दो मानवीय क्रियाओं को स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain any two human activities responsible for degradation of environment.

key_points: Industrialisation and burning of fossil fuels release greenhouse gases and pollutants, causing air pollution, acid rain, and global warming.
Deforestation for agriculture, urbanisation, and timber destroys ecosystems, reduces biodiversity, accelerates soil erosion, and contributes to climate change.

questions.solution: Two major human activities responsible for environmental degradation are industrialisation and deforestation. Rapid industrialisation involves burning fossil fuels which releases carbon dioxide, methane, and other greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, leading to air pollution, acid rain, and global warming. Second, large-scale deforestation — carried out to clear land for agriculture, urban expansion, and timber — destroys natural habitats, reduces biodiversity, causes soil erosion, disrupts the water cycle, and removes one of the most important carbon sinks, thereby accelerating climate change.
questions.solution_hindi: पर्यावरणीय निम्नीकरण के लिए उत्तरदायी दो प्रमुख मानवीय क्रियाएँ हैं — औद्योगीकरण और वनों की कटाई। तीव्र औद्योगीकरण में जीवाश्म ईंधन का उपयोग कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड और अन्य ग्रीनहाउस गैसें उत्सर्जित करता है जिससे वायु प्रदूषण, अम्लीय वर्षा और जलवायु परिवर्तन होता है। वनों की कटाई से जैव विविधता नष्ट होती है, मिट्टी का क्षरण होता है और जलवायु परिवर्तन में तेज़ी आती है।
questions.chapter: पर्यावरण और प्राकृतिक संसाधन / Environment and Natural Resources

questions.text: किन आधारों पर वैश्वीकरण को एक बहु-आयामी अवधारणा माना जा सकता है ? उदाहरण सहित व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: On what grounds can globalisation be considered a multi-dimensional concepts ? Explain with example.

key_points: Globalisation has economic dimensions — free trade, movement of capital, multinational corporations operating across borders.
Globalisation has political and cultural dimensions — spread of democratic values, human rights norms, and cultural exchange through media, internet, and migration.

questions.solution: Globalisation is a multi-dimensional concept because it operates simultaneously in economic, political, and cultural spheres. Economically, it involves the free movement of goods, capital, and services across borders — for example, multinational companies like McDonald's or Apple operating in virtually every country. Politically, it promotes the spread of democracy and human rights norms globally. Culturally, it leads to the exchange and blending of cultures through films, music, food, and social media — for instance, the worldwide popularity of Korean pop culture (K-pop). This multi-layered nature makes globalisation a complex, multi-dimensional phenomenon.
questions.solution_hindi: वैश्वीकरण एक बहु-आयामी अवधारणा है क्योंकि यह एक साथ आर्थिक, राजनीतिक और सांस्कृतिक क्षेत्रों में काम करती है। आर्थिक रूप से वस्तुओं और पूँजी का मुक्त प्रवाह होता है (जैसे — बहुराष्ट्रीय कंपनियाँ)। राजनीतिक रूप से लोकतंत्र और मानवाधिकार के मूल्यों का प्रसार होता है। सांस्कृतिक रूप से फिल्म, संगीत और इंटरनेट के माध्यम से संस्कृतियों का आदान-प्रदान होता है।
questions.chapter: वैश्वीकरण / Globalisation

questions.text: प्रधानमंत्री लाल बहादुर शास्त्री के कार्यकाल में भारत के समक्ष की किन्हीं दो चुनौतियों का वर्णन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Describe any two challenges faced by India during the term of Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri.

key_points: The Indo-Pakistan War of 1965 which posed a serious military and security challenge to India.
The severe food crisis and widespread drought of 1965-66 which threatened economic stability and food security.

questions.solution: During Lal Bahadur Shastri's brief tenure as Prime Minister (1964–1966), India faced two major challenges. The first was the Indo-Pakistan War of 1965, in which Pakistan launched a military offensive codenamed Operation Gibraltar in Kashmir. Shastri responded boldly by ordering Indian forces to cross the international border near Lahore, and the war ended with the Tashkent Agreement in January 1966. The second challenge was a severe food crisis caused by consecutive droughts and inadequate food production, which made India heavily dependent on food imports, especially under the PL-480 agreement with the United States.
questions.solution_hindi: लाल बहादुर शास्त्री के कार्यकाल (1964–1966) में भारत को दो प्रमुख चुनौतियों का सामना करना पड़ा। पहली — 1965 का भारत-पाकिस्तान युद्ध, जिसमें पाकिस्तान ने ऑपरेशन जिब्राल्टर से कश्मीर पर आक्रमण किया। शास्त्री ने सेना को अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सीमा पार करने का आदेश दिया और युद्ध ताशकंद समझौते से समाप्त हुआ। दूसरी — भीषण सूखे के कारण खाद्य संकट जिसने भारत को खाद्य आयात पर निर्भर बना दिया।
questions.chapter: एक दल के प्रभुत्व का दौर / Era of One-Party Dominance

questions.text: "1980 के दशक में विभिन्न क्षेत्रीय आकांक्षाओं की माँगें राष्ट्र-निर्माण की दिशा में एक कदम थीं ।" तर्क देकर कथन की पुष्टि कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: "The demands of various regional aspirations during 1980s was a step towards nation building." Support the statement with argument.

key_points: Regional demands for autonomy, cultural recognition, and equitable development represented legitimate aspirations that when addressed, strengthened democratic federalism.
Negotiations and accords like the Punjab Accord and Assam Accord showed that regional demands could be resolved through democratic dialogue, reinforcing national unity rather than fragmenting it.

questions.solution: The regional aspirations of the 1980s were actually a step toward nation building because they forced the Indian state to become more inclusive and responsive. Movements like those in Punjab and Assam were not secessionist at heart but demanded fair recognition of cultural identity, protection of local resources, and equitable development. When the government responded through accords such as the Rajiv-Longowal Accord and the Assam Accord, it demonstrated that diverse identities could be accommodated within a united India. This process of negotiation strengthened federalism and reinforced the democratic fabric of the nation.
questions.solution_hindi: 1980 के दशक की क्षेत्रीय आकांक्षाएँ राष्ट्र निर्माण की दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम थीं क्योंकि इन्होंने भारतीय राज्य को अधिक समावेशी बनाया। पंजाब और असम जैसे आंदोलन सांस्कृतिक पहचान और न्यायसंगत विकास की माँग कर रहे थे। पंजाब समझौते और असम समझौते जैसे प्रयासों ने यह सिद्ध किया कि लोकतांत्रिक संवाद से विविधता में एकता स्थापित की जा सकती है।
questions.chapter: लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था का संकट / Crisis of Democratic Order
questions.topic: Regional Aspirations and Nation Building in 1980s

questions.text: समाजवादी पार्टी और कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी ऑफ इंडिया की विचारधारा में कोई दो अंतर उजागर कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Highlight any two differences between the ideologies of Socialist party and Communist party of India.

key_points: The Socialist Party believed in achieving socialism through democratic and parliamentary means, whereas the Communist Party of India believed in revolutionary methods and was more closely aligned with the Soviet model of Marxist-Leninist ideology.

The Socialist Party was opposed to dependence on the Soviet Union and favoured an independent path; the CPI, especially in its early years, maintained close ideological ties with the Soviet Union and the international communist movement.

questions.solution: The Socialist Party and the Communist Party of India (CPI) both aimed for a just and equitable society but differed significantly in their approaches. First, the Socialist Party sought to achieve socialism through peaceful, democratic, and parliamentary means — working within the framework of electoral democracy and constitutional methods. In contrast, the Communist Party of India was more strongly influenced by Marxist-Leninist ideology and at times endorsed revolutionary mass mobilisation and class struggle as necessary instruments of change. Second, the Socialists were committed to non-alignment and independence from foreign influence in both policy and ideology. The CPI, however, maintained close ideological and organisational ties with the Soviet Union and the international communist movement, which often drew criticism that it was subordinating national interests to Soviet foreign policy objectives. These two differences defined the fundamental ideological divide between the two left-leaning parties in post-independence India.
questions.solution_hindi: समाजवादी पार्टी और कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी ऑफ इंडिया दोनों समतापूर्ण समाज चाहती थीं, लेकिन उनके तरीके अलग थे। पहला अंतर — समाजवादी पार्टी लोकतांत्रिक और संसदीय माध्यमों से समाजवाद स्थापित करना चाहती थी जबकि CPI मार्क्सवादी-लेनिनवादी क्रांतिकारी तरीकों में विश्वास रखती थी। दूसरा अंतर — समाजवादी पार्टी स्वतंत्र विचारधारा अपनाती थी जबकि CPI सोवियत संघ के साथ घनिष्ठ संबंध बनाए रखती थी।
questions.chapter: एक दल के प्रभुत्व का दौर / Era of One-Party Dominance
questions.topic: Socialist Party vs Communist Party of India

questions.text: विभिन्न देशों द्वारा अपनी राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा को बनाए रखने के लिए प्रयोग किए जा सकने वाले किन्हीं दो पारम्परिक उपायों को उजागर कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Highlight any two traditional measures which may be used by different countries to maintain their national security.

key_points: Military strengthening — building and maintaining armed forces, developing weapons systems, and increasing defence capabilities to deter aggression.
Alliance formation — entering into military alliances or security pacts with friendly nations to enhance collective security and deter potential threats.

questions.solution: Traditional security measures used by states to maintain national security fall broadly into two categories. The first is military strengthening, where a country invests in building and modernising its armed forces — army, navy, and air force — develops advanced weapons systems, maintains nuclear deterrence if applicable, and enhances border security infrastructure. This deters potential aggressors through the credible threat of retaliation. The second traditional measure is forming alliances with like-minded states. By entering into bilateral or multilateral defence agreements, a country enlarges its security umbrella. NATO is a classic example — member states commit to collective defence, meaning an attack on one is treated as an attack on all. Both measures have been the cornerstone of traditional security thinking in international relations.
questions.solution_hindi: राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा के दो प्रमुख पारम्परिक उपाय हैं। पहला — सैन्य शक्ति को मजबूत करना: थल सेना, नौसेना और वायु सेना का आधुनिकीकरण, परमाणु निरोधक क्षमता, और सीमा सुरक्षा ढाँचे का विकास। इससे आक्रमणकारियों को जवाबी कार्रवाई का भय रहता है। दूसरा — गठबंधन निर्माण: मित्र देशों के साथ द्विपक्षीय या बहुपक्षीय सुरक्षा संधियाँ करना। NATO इसका उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है।

questions.text: पर्यावरण की सुरक्षा के प्रति जागरूकता फैलाने के लिए पूरे विश्व में की गयी किन्हीं चार पहलों का वर्णन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Describe any four initiatives taken across the world to create awareness about the protection of the environment.

key_points: The United Nations Conference on Human Environment at Stockholm, 1972 — the first major international conference on environmental issues.
The Brundtland Commission Report (1987) 'Our Common Future' which coined the concept of sustainable development.
The Earth Summit at Rio de Janeiro, 1992 — led to Agenda 21 and commitments on climate change and biodiversity.
The Kyoto Protocol (1997) under which developed countries committed to reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

questions.solution: Four major global initiatives to create awareness about environmental protection are as follows. First, the United Nations Conference on Human Environment held at Stockholm in 1972 was the first major international gathering that brought governments together to address environmental degradation; it led to the creation of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). Second, the Brundtland Commission published its landmark report 'Our Common Future' in 1987, which popularised the concept of sustainable development — meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs. Third, the Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 produced Agenda 21, a comprehensive action plan for sustainable development, and opened the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). Fourth, the Kyoto Protocol of 1997 was a binding agreement under the UNFCCC in which industrialised nations committed to specific, measurable reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, representing the most concrete international legal step toward combating climate change.
questions.solution_hindi: पर्यावरण संरक्षण के प्रति जागरूकता के लिए विश्व में चार प्रमुख पहलें की गई हैं। पहली — 1972 का स्टॉकहोम सम्मेलन जो पर्यावरण पर पहला बड़ा अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सम्मेलन था और जिसके परिणामस्वरूप UNEP की स्थापना हुई। दूसरी — 1987 में ब्रुंडटलैंड आयोग की रिपोर्ट 'हमारा साझा भविष्य' जिसने सतत विकास की अवधारणा दी। तीसरी — 1992 का रियो पृथ्वी शिखर सम्मेलन जिसने एजेंडा 21 और UNFCCC को जन्म दिया। चौथी — 1997 का क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल जिसमें विकसित देशों ने ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन घटाने का बाध्यकारी संकल्प लिया।

sub_questions.text_english: "India has accepted expressions of regional aspirations to strengthen the national integrity." Support the statement with two examples.

key_points: The linguistic reorganisation of states in 1956 on the basis of the States Reorganisation Act, accepting demands for Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat etc., showed India accommodating regional cultural identities.
The Assam Accord (1985) and the Punjab Accord (Rajiv-Longowal Accord, 1985) where the central government negotiated settlements with regional movements to address their grievances peacefully.

sub_questions.solution: India's approach to regional aspirations has generally been one of accommodation rather than confrontation, thereby strengthening national unity. The first example is the linguistic reorganisation of states in 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, which accepted the popular demand for states based on language. The creation of Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, and other states showed that regional cultural identities could be acknowledged within a unified nation. The second example is the Assam Accord of 1985, in which the central government negotiated with the All Assam Students Union (AASU) to address the problem of illegal immigration. By committing to identify and deport illegal migrants, the government accepted the regional concern and brought the agitation to a peaceful end, demonstrating that regional aspirations, when addressed democratically, reinforce rather than weaken national integrity.

sub_questions.text: क्या आप सहमत हैं कि असम समझौता राज्य में शांति और स्थिरता लाने में सफल रहा ? अपने उत्तर के पक्ष में कोई दो तर्क दीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Do you agree that the Assam accord was successful in establishing peace and stability in the State ? Support your answer with any two arguments.

key_points: The Assam Accord (1985) successfully ended the six-year-long agitation by AASU, leading to elections and the formation of the Asom Gana Parishad government, restoring democratic normalcy.

However, the accord had limitations — the implementation of clauses regarding detection and deportation of illegal immigrants remained incomplete, leading to renewed tensions and the rise of the ULFA insurgency.

sub_questions.solution: The Assam Accord of 1985, signed between the Rajiv Gandhi government and the All Assam Students Union (AASU), had mixed success in bringing peace and stability to the state. In favour of its success, the Accord ended the six-year-long agitation that had claimed many lives and disrupted normal life. It led to fresh elections in which the Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) came to power, restoring democratic governance and giving regional aspirations a legitimate political outlet. This was a significant achievement. However, the Accord was not entirely successful because its key provision — identifying and deporting illegal immigrants who entered after 1971 — was never fully implemented due to practical and political difficulties. This failure bred continued resentment, which contributed to the emergence of the ULFA insurgency and persistent ethnic tensions in the state. Thus, while the Accord brought short-term stability, its incomplete implementation limited its long-term success.

sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the 'ASEAN way' as a unique initiative of promoting peace in South-east Asian Countries.

key_points: The 'ASEAN Way' refers to a style of interaction that emphasises informality, consensus, non-confrontation, and non-interference in internal affairs of member states.
It promotes conflict resolution through quiet diplomacy, dialogue, and consultation rather than confrontation, making it a unique model for peaceful coexistence in Southeast Asia.

sub_questions.solution: The 'ASEAN Way' refers to the distinctive approach to international relations and conflict resolution adopted by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. It is characterised by informality, consensus-based decision-making, and a strict principle of non-interference in the internal affairs of member states. Unlike Western multilateral institutions that often use formal, legalistic, and confrontational mechanisms, ASEAN prefers quiet diplomacy, patient consultation, and confidence-building measures. This approach has been unique and effective in a region marked by diverse political systems — from democracies to authoritarian regimes — and historical border disputes. By emphasising dialogue over confrontation, the ASEAN Way has helped prevent military conflicts among member states since its founding in 1967 and created a regional culture of peaceful cooperation that is widely respected as a model for other developing regions.

sub_questions.text: अपनी आर्थिक प्रगति की वृद्धि में 'आसियान सुरक्षा समुदाय' के योगदान का निर्धारण कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Determine the contribution of 'ASEAN security community' in its promotion of economic progress.

key_points: By maintaining regional peace and stability, the ASEAN Security Community created a safe environment that attracted foreign direct investment and enabled sustained economic growth.
The security framework allowed member states to focus resources on economic development rather than arms races, facilitating the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) and deeper economic integration.

sub_questions.solution: The ASEAN Security Community (ASC) has made important contributions to the economic progress of member states by creating and sustaining the conditions necessary for economic development. By resolving or managing regional disputes peacefully and preventing interstate military conflicts, the ASC provided the political stability that is a prerequisite for investor confidence. Foreign direct investment flowed into Southeast Asia partly because multinational corporations viewed the region as stable and predictable. The security cooperation also reduced the burden of excessive military spending on member economies, freeing up public resources for infrastructure, education, and industrial development. Furthermore, the security framework provided the political foundation upon which the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) was built, enabling trade liberalisation and deeper economic integration. Countries like Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia emerged as significant economic players in the global economy in part because of the stable regional security environment that ASEAN helped maintain.

questions.text:

दक्षेस (साउथ एशियन एसोसिएशन फॉर रीजनल को-ऑपरेशन (SAARC)) दक्षिण एशियाई देशों द्वारा बहुतरीय साधनों से आपस में सहयोग करने की दिशा में उठाया गया बड़ा कदम है । इसकी शुरुआत 1985 में हुई । दुर्भाग्य से विभेदों की मौजूदगी के कारण दक्षेस को ज्यादा सफलता नहीं मिली । दक्षेस के सदस्य देशों ने सन् 2002 में दक्षिण एशियाई मुक्त व्यापार-क्षेत्र समझौते (SAFTA) पर दस्तखत किये । जिसमें पूरे दक्षिण एशिया के लिए मुक्त व्यापार क्षेत्र बनाने का वादा है ।
questions.text_english: The South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC) is a major regional initiative by the South Asian states to evolve co-operation through multilateral means. It began in 1985. Unfortunately due to persisting political differences, SAARC has not had much success. SAARC members signed the South Asian Free Trade Agreement (SAFTA) in 2002 which promised the formation of a free trade zone for the whole of South Asia.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा दक्षिण एशियाई देश दक्षेस का संस्थापक देश नहीं है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following South Asian countries is not a founder member of South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC) ?
sub_questions.solution: Afghanistan is not a founder member of SAARC. SAARC was founded in 1985 by seven countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Afghanistan was admitted as the eighth member only in 2007. Therefore option (C) is correct.

sub_questions.text: कौन सी बाहरी ताकत दक्षिण एशियाई देशों पर सर्वाधिक प्रभाव डालती है ?

sub_questions.solution: The United States of America (option A) is the external power that most significantly affects South Asian countries through its economic aid, military relationships, strategic partnerships (particularly with India and Pakistan), and its dominant role in international financial institutions like the IMF and World Bank. The US influence is particularly visible in the Pakistan-India-US triangle of relations.

sub_questions.text: दक्षिण एशियाई क्षेत्रीय सहयोग संगठन (सार्क) का प्रमुख उद्देश्य क्या है ?
sub_questions.text_english: The major objective of South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation is –

options.A: विश्व में समकालीन सत्ता का केन्द्र बनना ।
options.B: अपने आर्थिक विकास के लिए क्षेत्रीय संगठन की एक साझी मुद्रा स्थापित करना ।
options.C: बाहरी ताकतों के हस्तक्षेप के बिना क्षेत्रीय संघर्षों का समाधान करना ।
options.D: सदस्य देशों के आर्थिक विकास, सामाजिक प्रगति और सांस्कृतिक विकास के लिए बहुतरीय माध्यमों से सहयोग करना ।

options_english.A: To become a contemporary centre of power in the World.
options_english.B: To establish a common currency for the regional organisation for its economic development.
options_english.C: To solve all regional conflicts without interference of external powers.
options_english.D: To co-operate member states for economic growth, social progress and cultural development through multilateral means.

sub_questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. As stated in the SAARC Charter, the primary objective of the organisation is to promote the welfare of the peoples of South Asia, accelerate economic growth, social progress and cultural development, and provide every individual the opportunity to live in dignity — all through multilateral cooperation among member states.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा उद्देश्य दक्षिण एशियाई मुक्त व्यापार समझौते (साफ्टा) का मुख्य उद्देश्य नहीं है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following is NOT a core objective of South Asian Free Trade Agreement (SAFTA) ?

options.A: सार्क देशों के लिए साझी मुद्रा स्थापित करना ।
options.B: आपसी व्यापार और आर्थिक सहयोग का प्रसार करना और बढ़ावा देना ।
options.C: सीमा-शुल्क और गैर-शुल्क बाधाओं को कम करना ।
options.D: सदस्य देशों के मध्य एक मुक्त व्यापार का क्षेत्र बनाना ।

options_english.A: To establish a common currency for SAARC nations.
options_english.B: To promote and enhance mutual trade and economic co-operation.
options_english.C: To reduce custom duties and non-tariff barriers.
options_english.D: To create a free trade area among member states.

sub_questions.solution: Option (A) is the correct answer (i.e., NOT an objective). SAFTA's objectives are focused on trade liberalisation — reducing tariffs and non-tariff barriers, promoting mutual trade, and creating a free trade area in South Asia. Establishing a common currency like the Euro is not among SAFTA's objectives; that would require a much deeper level of monetary integration that SAARC has not envisaged.

sub_questions.solution: The Prince sitting on the back of a poor common man symbolises the exploitative and oppressive nature of princely rule. It indicates that the rulers of princely states lived in luxury and exercised autocratic power at the expense of the ordinary people, who were burdened and subjugated under their rule. It critiques the feudal character of the princely order.

sub_questions.text: कार्टून द्वारा क्या संदेश दिया गया है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What message is being conveyed by the cartoon ?

key_points: Sardar Patel's pragmatic and diplomatic approach to integration — he asked for only the three key subjects (external affairs, defence, communications) rather than full political subjugation.
The cartoon critiques the feudal burden of princely rule on ordinary people and highlights the political wisdom of negotiated integration over confrontation.

sub_questions.solution: The cartoon conveys two important messages about the integration of princely states. First, it highlights Sardar Patel's pragmatic diplomatic strategy — rather than demanding the complete and immediate surrender of all powers, he wisely asked the princes to cede only three essential subjects: external affairs, defence, and communications. This approach reduced resistance and made integration possible without widespread conflict. Second, the cartoon critiques the exploitative feudal order by showing the prince riding on the back of a poor man, representing the common people. The message is that the princes' authority rested on the suffering of ordinary subjects, and integration with democratic India would ultimately liberate them from this burden.

(a) संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ के किन्हीं तीन अंगों की संरचना और उनके एक-एक कार्य को स्पष्ट कीजिए ।

अथवा

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain the composition and one function of any three organs of the United Nations.

OR

(b) Name any three agencies of the United Nations and explain one function of each.

sub_questions.text: संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ के किन्हीं तीन अंगों की संरचना और उनके एक-एक कार्य को स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the composition and one function of any three organs of the United Nations.

key_points: General Assembly — composed of all 193 member states, each with one vote; function: debates and passes resolutions on international peace, security, development, and other global issues.

Security Council — composed of 15 members: 5 permanent (USA, UK, France, Russia, China) with veto power and 10 non-permanent elected for 2-year terms; function: primary responsibility for international peace and security, can authorise military action and impose sanctions.
International Court of Justice (ICJ) — composed of 15 judges elected for 9-year terms; function: settles legal disputes between states and gives advisory opinions on international legal questions.

sub_questions.solution: The United Nations has six principal organs. Three of the most important are described below. First, the General Assembly is composed of all 193 member states of the UN, with each state having one vote regardless of size or power. Its primary function is to serve as a deliberative forum where all global issues — from peace and security to development and human rights — can be discussed and resolutions passed, though these resolutions are non-binding on member states. Second, the Security Council consists of 15 members: five permanent members — the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, and China — who hold veto power, and ten non-permanent members elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms. Its principal function is to maintain international peace and security; it can investigate disputes, recommend peaceful solutions, authorise peacekeeping missions, impose economic sanctions, and even authorise military action against aggressors. Third, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is the principal judicial organ of the UN, composed of 15 judges elected jointly by the General Assembly and Security Council for nine-year terms. Its function is to settle legal disputes submitted by states and to give advisory opinions on international legal questions referred by UN organs.

sub_questions.text: संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ की किन्हीं तीन एजेंसियों के नाम लिखकर उनके एक-एक कार्य की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Name any three agencies of the United Nations and explain one function of each.

key_points: WHO (World Health Organisation) — coordinates international public health responses, sets health standards, and leads vaccination and disease eradication programmes.
UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation) — promotes international cooperation in education, science, and culture; designates World Heritage Sites.
UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund) — works to protect the rights of children globally, provides humanitarian aid to children in conflict zones, and promotes child education and healthcare.

sub_questions.solution: Three important agencies of the United Nations and their functions are as follows. The first is the World Health Organisation (WHO), established in 1948 and headquartered in Geneva. It coordinates the international community's response to global public health emergencies, sets international health standards, leads global vaccination campaigns, and works to eradicate deadly diseases. Its response to the COVID-19 pandemic and earlier leadership in eradicating smallpox are notable examples of its work. The second agency is UNESCO — the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation — which promotes international cooperation in education, science, and culture. One of its important functions is the designation of UNESCO World Heritage Sites, which protects cultural and natural landmarks of outstanding universal value across the globe. The third agency is UNICEF — the United Nations Children's Fund — which works to protect the rights, health, and welfare of children worldwide. Its key function is to provide humanitarian assistance to children in conflict zones and natural disasters, deliver essential vaccines, and promote universal primary education for all children, particularly girls in developing countries.

(b) शॉक थेरेपी के किन्हीं तीन परिणामों की परख कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Analyse any three reasons for the disintegration of the Soviet Union.

OR

(b) Examine any three consequences of the Shock therapy.

sub_questions.text: सोवियत संघ के विघटन के किन्हीं तीन कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse any three reasons for the disintegration of the Soviet Union.

key_points: Economic stagnation — the Soviet command economy failed to match Western living standards, suffered from inefficiency, technological backwardness, and inability to satisfy consumer demand.

Rise of nationalism — constituent republics like Ukraine, Georgia, and the Baltic states increasingly asserted their national identities and demanded independence, overwhelming the central Soviet authority.

Political reforms backfiring — Gorbachev's glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring) policies, while intended to revitalise the Soviet system, inadvertently unleashed forces of political liberalisation and nationalism that the Communist Party could not control.

sub_questions.solution: Three major reasons for the disintegration of the Soviet Union in 1991 can be analysed as follows. The first and most fundamental reason was economic stagnation. The Soviet command economy, which had delivered impressive growth in the early decades, had become deeply inefficient by the 1980s. It could not generate enough consumer goods, suffered from technological backwardness compared to the West, and was spending enormous resources on the arms race. The resulting decline in living standards eroded public confidence in the Soviet system. The second reason was the rise of strong nationalist movements within the constituent republics. Countries like Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Ukraine, and Georgia increasingly asserted their distinct national and cultural identities. These republics demanded greater autonomy and eventually full independence, and the central Soviet government could not suppress these aspirations by force without enormous political cost. Third, Mikhail Gorbachev's reform policies of glasnost (political openness) and perestroika (economic restructuring), though well-intentioned, accelerated the Soviet collapse. Glasnost allowed free expression of criticism of the Communist Party and government, exposing decades of mismanagement and human rights abuses. Perestroika introduced market elements but created confusion and economic disruption. Together, these reforms opened a political space that nationalist and reform movements exploited to challenge the party's monopoly on power, ultimately leading to the collapse of the USSR in December 1991.

sub_questions.text: शॉक थेरेपी के किन्हीं तीन परिणामों की परख कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Examine any three consequences of the Shock therapy.

key_points: Economic collapse and widespread poverty — the rapid dismantling of the command economy without adequate replacement institutions led to factory closures, unemployment, and a dramatic fall in GDP in Russia and Eastern Europe.
Rise of oligarchs — privatisation of state assets at rock-bottom prices allowed a small group of well-connected individuals to acquire enormous wealth, creating extreme inequality.
Social hardship — collapse of the social safety net led to a rise in poverty, unemployment, health problems, reduced life expectancy, and widespread social dislocation.

sub_questions.solution: Shock Therapy was the rapid, comprehensive economic transformation programme prescribed by Western advisers and international financial institutions for post-Soviet Russia and Eastern Europe. Three major consequences of this policy were as follows. The first consequence was economic devastation. The abrupt dismantling of state enterprises, removal of price controls, and overnight privatisation led to massive factory closures, soaring unemployment, and hyperinflation. Russia's GDP fell drastically in the 1990s — some estimates suggest it declined by nearly 50% — plunging millions into poverty. The second consequence was the creation of extreme inequality and the rise of oligarchs. State assets were sold at artificially low prices in rushed privatisations, allowing a small group of politically connected businessmen to acquire enormous wealth almost overnight. This created a class of oligarchs who came to dominate both the economy and politics, undermining the prospects for genuine democratic capitalism. The third consequence was severe social hardship. The collapse of the Soviet-era social safety net — which had guaranteed employment, housing, healthcare, and basic food — left ordinary citizens without a support system. Life expectancy in Russia fell sharply, poverty increased dramatically, crime rose, and a sense of social dislocation and disillusionment spread across former Soviet societies. These consequences made Shock Therapy deeply unpopular and widely regarded as having failed the people of the former Soviet bloc.

(a) "भारत की विदेश नीति अपने 'राष्ट्रीय हितों' की रक्षा में सफल रही है ।" कथन के पक्ष में तीन तर्क दीजिए ।

questions.text_english:
(a) "India's Foreign Policy has been successful in saving its 'National Interests'." Support the statement with three arguments.

OR

(b) "India's Foreign Policy is as per the principles of International Peace and Security as laid down in Article 51 of the Indian Constitution." Justify the statement with three examples.

sub_questions.text: "भारत की विदेश नीति अपने 'राष्ट्रीय हितों' की रक्षा में सफल रही है ।" कथन के पक्ष में तीन तर्क दीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: "India's Foreign Policy has been successful in saving its 'National Interests'." Support the statement with three arguments.

key_points: Non-Alignment helped India secure economic and military aid from both superpowers while maintaining strategic autonomy during the Cold War.
India successfully resisted pressure to sign the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) which it considered discriminatory, protecting its right to develop nuclear capabilities.
India's foreign policy successfully managed the liberation of Bangladesh in 1971 through the Indo-Soviet Treaty, securing its eastern flank and reshaping South Asian geopolitics in its favour.

sub_questions.solution: India's foreign policy, rooted in the principles of Panchsheel and Non-Alignment, has been broadly successful in protecting its national interests, as three arguments demonstrate. First, the policy of Non-Alignment during the Cold War allowed India to maintain its strategic independence while extracting maximum benefit from both superpower blocs. India received military equipment from the Soviet Union and economic and technological assistance from the United States and Western countries, without being subordinated to either bloc's political objectives. This preserved India's sovereignty and accelerated its development. Second, India successfully resisted intense international pressure to sign the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), which India consistently criticised as discriminatory because it allowed the five permanent members of the UN Security Council to retain nuclear weapons while denying this right to others. By refusing to sign and eventually conducting nuclear tests in 1974 and 1998, India secured its nuclear deterrent — a crucial national interest given its security environment with China and Pakistan. Third, in 1971, India's foreign policy demonstrated remarkable strategic success in the Bangladesh Liberation War. The timely signing of the Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation provided India with diplomatic and military cover against possible American or Chinese intervention. This allowed India to assist the liberation of Bangladesh, defeat Pakistan militarily, and reshape the geopolitical balance in South Asia decisively in India's favour — a landmark achievement of national interest.

sub_questions.text: "भारत की विदेश नीति भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 51 में वर्णित अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति और स्थिरता के सिद्धान्तों के अनुरूप है ।" तीन उदाहरणों से इस कथन को सही ठहराइये ।
sub_questions.text_english: "India's Foreign Policy is as per the principles of International Peace and Security as laid down in Article 51 of the Indian Constitution." Justify the statement with three examples.

key_points: India's policy of Non-Alignment and active promotion of disarmament reflects Article 51's mandate to promote international peace.
India's participation in UN peacekeeping missions across the world reflects the Article 51 commitment to settling international disputes peacefully.
India's role in the Non-Aligned Movement and advocacy for a New International Economic Order aligned with the Article 51 principle of fostering respect for international law and treaty obligations.

sub_questions.solution: Article 51 of the Indian Constitution directs the state to promote international peace and security, maintain just and honourable relations between nations, foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and encourage settlement of disputes by arbitration. India's foreign policy reflects these principles through three concrete examples. First, India's founding role in the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) in 1961 directly embodies Article 51. Under Nehru's leadership, India refused to join either Cold War military bloc and instead championed peaceful coexistence through the Panchsheel principles — mutual respect, non-aggression, non-interference, equality, and peaceful coexistence. This represented a practical commitment to international peace that earned India global moral authority. Second, India has been one of the largest contributors to United Nations peacekeeping operations since the 1950s, sending troops to the Congo, Korea, Lebanon, Cambodia, and numerous other conflict zones. This participation directly reflects the Article 51 commitment to resolving international disputes through multilateral, peaceful means rather than unilateral military action. Third, India consistently advocated for nuclear disarmament and proposed the elimination of nuclear weapons through its various disarmament initiatives in the UN. India's Rajiv Gandhi Action Plan for disarmament (1988) called for a phased and time-bound elimination of nuclear weapons globally, demonstrating adherence to the Article 51 principle of fostering international peace through arms control.

questions.text:
(a) 1989 के पश्चात् केंद्र में गठबंधन की सरकारों के उदय के लिए उत्तरदायी किन्हीं चार कारकों का वर्णन कीजिए ।

अथवा

(b) ऐसे किन्हीं चार मुद्दों का वर्णन कीजिए जिन पर अधिकांश राजनीतिक पार्टियों के बीच एक व्यापक सहमति दिखाई देती है ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Describe any four factors responsible for the rise of coalition governments at the centre after the year 1989.

OR

(b) Describe any four issues on which a broad agreement has emerged among most political parties.

sub_questions.text: 1989 के पश्चात् केंद्र में गठबंधन की सरकारों के उदय के लिए उत्तरदायी किन्हीं चार कारकों का वर्णन कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any four factors responsible for the rise of coalition governments at the centre after the year 1989.

key_points: Decline of Congress dominance — the Congress party lost its position as the dominant single-party force, making majority governments increasingly difficult.
Rise of regional parties — strong state-level parties like the Samajwadi Party, DMK, TDP, and Shiv Sena began winning significant numbers of seats, fragmenting the Lok Sabha.
Increased political mobilisation of OBCs, Dalits, and minorities — the Mandal Commission implementation empowered new social groups who supported regional/caste-based parties rather than Congress.
Electoral system and social diversity — India's first-past-the-post system combined with its immense social diversity produced a fragmented legislature where no single party could secure a majority.

sub_questions.solution: After the 1989 general elections, India entered an era of coalition politics at the centre, with no single party winning an outright majority for nearly three decades. Four factors responsible for this transition are as follows. First, the decline of the Congress party's dominance was a critical factor. The Congress had governed India for most of the period since independence, often winning commanding majorities. However, corruption scandals, the fallout of the Emergency, the Bofors controversy, and growing voter discontent eroded Congress's mass base, making it unable to win outright majorities. Second, the rise of regional parties transformed Indian politics. Parties like the Telugu Desam Party, the Samajwadi Party, the Bahujan Samaj Party, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, and the Shiv Sena built strong state-level followings. In the Lok Sabha, they won dozens of seats each, making it impossible for national parties to form governments without their support. Third, the implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations in 1990, which provided reservations to Other Backward Classes (OBCs), dramatically increased the political mobilisation of OBCs, Dalits, and other marginalised communities. These groups increasingly supported regional and caste-based parties rather than the Congress, further fragmenting the vote. Fourth, the sheer social diversity of India — with its multiple linguistic, religious, caste, and regional identities — combined with the first-past-the-post electoral system produced a naturally fragmented Lok Sabha in which multiple competing interests sought parliamentary representation. This structural reality made single-party majority governments increasingly rare and coalition arrangements the norm.

sub_questions.text: ऐसे किन्हीं चार मुद्दों का वर्णन कीजिए जिन पर अधिकांश राजनीतिक पार्टियों के बीच एक व्यापक सहमति दिखाई देती है ।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any four issues on which a broad agreement has emerged among most political parties.

key_points: New economic policies — most parties broadly accept the framework of economic liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation initiated in 1991, differing mainly on pace and implementation.
Accommodation of backward castes — all major parties accept the need for reservations and affirmative action for OBCs, SCs, and STs as a legitimate policy tool.
Acceptance of federalism — all parties broadly agree on the importance of states' rights and cooperative federalism, opposing excessive centralisation.

National security — there is a broad consensus across parties on maintaining strong national defence, not compromising on nuclear capabilities, and on the resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir issue within the constitutional framework.

sub_questions.solution: Despite the intense competition among India's political parties, a broad consensus has emerged on several important issues. Four such areas of agreement are as follows. First, there is a broad consensus on new economic policies. While parties may debate the pace or extent of reforms, virtually all major parties — from the BJP and Congress to regional parties — have accepted the basic framework of economic liberalisation, privatisation, and integration into the global economy that was initiated in 1991. Even the Left, which opposes certain aspects, has not reversed these policies when in power in states. Second, most parties agree on the accommodation of backward classes. The implementation of Mandal Commission recommendations created a political consensus that affirmative action and reservations for OBCs, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes are legitimate, necessary, and politically non-negotiable policies. No mainstream party openly opposes reservations. Third, there is consensus on federalism and the importance of states. All parties — particularly regional ones but also national parties — broadly agree that India's federal structure should be respected, that states should have adequate financial and legislative autonomy, and that excessive centralisation is undesirable. Fourth, most parties share a consensus on issues of national security and territorial integrity. There is broad agreement that India's nuclear deterrent should be maintained, that the borders of India should not be compromised, and that insurgencies or secessionist movements should be resolved within the constitutional framework — even if parties disagree on specific tactics.
